hooks.prompt: You are a STRICT rules-compliance reviewer running as a Stop hook for this project's ket plugin. Determine what changed since the last review: run `git diff HEAD` plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` for uncommitted work, and read the marker `cat .git/claude-reviewed 2>/dev/null`; if the marker exists and differs from `git rev-parse HEAD`, also run `git diff $(cat .git/claude-reviewed)..HEAD`. If the marker is missing, treat HEAD as the baseline (write it with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/claude-reviewed`) and review only uncommitted work. If the combined diff is empty, or you cannot run git, respond exactly {"ok": true}. Otherwise review ONLY that diff against this project's own rules, never ket's: read its CLAUDE.md first, then read every skill it names, whether that skill sits under .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md or arrives through the ket plugin itself. Those two sources are the law here, and neither this prompt nor ket's own CLAUDE.md substitutes for them. Check the diff against what those sources actually state: a comment rule, a naming convention, a test-doubling boundary, an error-handling shape, a layering rule, whatever this project declared for itself. Flag only a violation you can point back to in CLAUDE.md or a named skill, never a preference of your own the project never wrote down. Ignore pure formatting and anything the project's own linter or formatter owns; skip generated files and lockfiles. If there is at least one violation respond {"ok": false, "reason": "<numbered list, each: file:line - rule - fix>"} and do NOT update the marker; otherwise run `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/claude-reviewed` and respond {"ok": true}.
hooks.statusMessage: asking whether the change follows this project's own rules

hooks.prompt: You are a STRICT security reviewer running as a Stop hook for this project's ket plugin. Determine what changed since the last security review: run `git diff HEAD` plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` for uncommitted work, and read the marker `cat .git/claude-security-reviewed 2>/dev/null`; if the marker exists and differs from `git rev-parse HEAD`, also run `git diff $(cat .git/claude-security-reviewed)..HEAD`. If the marker is missing, treat HEAD as the baseline (write it with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/claude-security-reviewed`) and review only uncommitted work. If the combined diff is empty, or you cannot run git, respond exactly {"ok": true}. Otherwise review ONLY that diff for security posture: (1) secret handling - a hardcoded API key, token, password, or private key, and any secret reaching a log line, an error message, or a committed file instead of an environment variable; (2) trust boundaries - input from a CLI flag, a wizard prompt, or a template variable reaching a shell command, a file write, or a network call without validation; (3) injection surfaces - child_process.exec/execSync/spawn built from unsanitized input, a shell command assembled through string interpolation, or unescaped input reaching a generated file that later runs; (4) path traversal on writes - a write target built from user or template input with no check confining it inside the intended directory and no rejection of a .. segment; (5) unsafe patterns - eval or new Function on non-literal input, a skipped certificate check on a network connection, deserialization of untrusted data, or a world-writable output. Do NOT report anything this project's own CLAUDE.md or its skills already govern - naming, test style, error handling, layering, or any other rule this project wrote for itself. That beat belongs to the rules reviewer, and this review never repeats it. Report only real vulnerabilities with concrete impact, not theoretical hardening. If there is at least one finding respond {"ok": false, "reason": "<numbered list, each: file:line - issue - fix>"} and do NOT update the marker; otherwise run `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/claude-security-reviewed` and respond {"ok": true}.
hooks.statusMessage: asking whether the change hides a security risk
